title: The reactor's default database is an ephemeral in-memory PGlite; persistence requires an explicit choice
content:
Build a reactor with nothing but document models registered and you get an **in-memory** PGlite database. The builder calls an internal `createDefaultDatabase()` that constructs `new Kysely({ dialect: new PGliteDialect(new PGlite()) })` — and `new PGlite()` with no arguments is in-memory. Nothing is written to disk and nothing survives the process.

```typescript
const reactor = await new ReactorBuilder()
  .withDocumentModelSources([myDocumentModel])
  .build();
```

`buildModule()` picks the base database in a strict precedence order:

1. The instance passed to `withKysely(...)`, if any.
2. A Postgres pool, if the worker pool is enabled and a worker `db` config is set.
3. The in-memory PGlite default.

So persistence is never inferred — there is no auto-detection, no environment sniffing. If you did not pass a Kysely instance or a worker-pool `db`, your data is gone at process exit. That is the correct backend for unit tests and local development (fresh isolated database every run, no external service), and a silent data-loss bug in anything else.

What you get on the default path: migrations run automatically (strategy defaults to `"auto"`, running `runMigrations(db, REACTOR_SCHEMA)`), all storage under the `"reactor"` Postgres schema, a single in-process executor (`maxConcurrency` defaults to `1`), an in-process read-model coordinator, and `module.pools === []` since there is no `pg.Pool` to instrument.

Move to Postgres when state must survive a restart, when more than one process must share storage, or when you scale — and note that **neither scaling path can run on PGlite at all**, because PGlite cannot be shared across threads. Both `withWorkerPool` and `withProjectionShards` therefore require a real Postgres server.

For `"manual"` or `"none"` migration strategies, run migrations yourself. `runMigrations` never throws on a migration error — it returns `{ success, migrationsExecuted, error? }`, so you must check the result:

```typescript
const result = await runMigrations(db, REACTOR_SCHEMA);
if (!result.success && result.error) throw result.error;
```

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/01-Reactor/07-StorageAndScaling.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: Precedence in buildModule(): withKysely instance, then the worker pool's Postgres db, then in-memory PGlite. Nothing survives the process on the default path.
